nota: F150–F152, N009 relidos. PENDENTE f137, ACHADO: 'Of 606 jellyfish stings documented, 225 were confirmed to have been caused by C. fleckeri' (as 225 'were stung in Darwin Harbour or the Tiwi Islands and were thus classified as C. fleckeri envenoming'); 'Cardiorespiratory arrest occurred within several minutes of the sting in the one fatal case, involving a 3-year-old girl'; período 'between 1 April 1991 and 30 May 2004'. Logo, 1 morte em 225 picadas CONFIRMADAS (0.44 %): é letalidade entre os picados que chegaram ao serviço, não risco por banhista. Na tela, se for: '1 DEATH IN 225 CONFIRMED STINGS · DARWIN AREA, 1991–2004'. A temporada: '92% occurred during the "stinger season" (1 October to 1 June)'.

texto_aprovado: It's in the water, and it comes with a season. By a 2005 count, the box jellyfish had been blamed for around 70 deaths in tropical Australian waters over the years. It starts life as tiny polyps in tidal creeks, and it comes out to sea at the start of each "stinger season," which runs from October to June.
